subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session authorization fail closed on all legacy ownerless rows, and should this PR become the canonical shared guard for the overlapping sessions.patch work?
rationale: Exact equality closes the demonstrated cross-owner path, but it also revokes previously working access to persisted ownerless sessions and establishes a permanent plugin-runtime authorization contract that repository policy reserves for explicit owner judgment.

options.title: Strict shared boundary
options.body: Require exact owner equality for create, patch, reset, and delete, consolidate the overlapping PR onto one helper, and add upgrade plus live-runtime proof.

options.title: Migrate legacy ownership
options.body: Define a narrow doctor or migration path that assigns or quarantines legacy ownerless plugin sessions before enabling strict runtime rejection.

options.title: Decline per-plugin isolation
options.body: Treat installed plugins as sharing the Gateway trust boundary and close or narrow both PRs rather than introducing owner-based runtime authorization.

recommendation.title: Strict shared boundary
recommendation.body: Require exact owner equality for create, patch, reset, and delete, consolidate the overlapping PR onto one helper, and add upgrade plus live-runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman's recent session-ownership and persistence work is the strongest history signal for deciding the legacy-row and shared-helper contract.
